proposal.summary: Server-side request forgery (SSRF) in CONPROSYS HMI System (CHS) versions prior to 3.5.3 allows a user with administrative privilege to bypass database restriction on the query setting page and connect to an unintended database.
proposal.affected_product: CONPROSYS HMI System (CHS) versions prior to 3.5.3
proposal.cwe_quote: Server-side request forgery vulnerability exists in CONPROSYS HMI System (CHS) versions prior to 3.5.3.

PR.quote: A user who can access the affected product with an administrative privilege may bypass the database restriction set on the query setting page, and connect to a user unintended database.

C.quote: A user who can access the affected product with an administrative privilege may bypass the database restriction set on the query setting page, and connect to a user unintended database.

I.quote: A user who can access the affected product with an administrative privilege may bypass the database restriction set on the query setting page, and connect to a user unintended database.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Attempt to reproduce the SSRF against affected versions (pre-3.5.3), capture a proof-of-concept request showing access to unintended databases, and request a vendor patch or mitigation. Collect logs and impacted database identifiers to assess data exposure.

evidence_quotes.quote: Server-side request forgery vulnerability exists in CONPROSYS HMI System (CHS) versions prior to 3.5.3.
A user who can access the affected product with an administrative privilege may bypass the database restriction set on the query setting page, and connect to a user unintended database.
